newsitem.title: CANADA: Oxford, GE Capital win Prudential deal.
newsitem.headline: Oxford, GE Capital win Prudential deal.

text.p: The Prudential Insurance Co of America said on Monday its Canadian unit has agreed to sell its Canadian real estate portfolio to a 50/50 joint venture of Oxford Properties Group Inc and GE Capital Canada Inc for C$455.8 million.
The 48 properties in the portfolio consist of five Toronto land parcels and 43 commercial properties across Canada comprising about 5.6 million square feet of rentable area.
The Oxford/GE bid was chosen after a competitive bidding process whose deadline was July 16.
The deal is slated to close in mid September.
Shares of Oxford rose 0.40 to 34.00 in Toronto Stock Exchange trading of more than 7000 shares in the wake of the agreement..

"They (Oxford and GE) were probably considered by many to be the front runners in the bidding process so I don't think it really comes as a shock," Mike Hough, a real estate analyst with HSBC James Capel Canada, told Reuters. "They do have tremendous capital resources and access to capital markets."
TrizecHahn Corp and Dundee Realty D.TO Corp were also reported to have bid on the properties.

The acquisition of the Prudential portfolio is the second major acquisition by Oxford and GE Capital -- a unit of General Electric Co -- in the past year. Last September Oxford and GE bought most of Canadian Pacific Ltd's real estate portfolio for C$952 million including assumed debt.

Prior to the Prudential acquisition, Oxford owned a net 7.9 million square foot interest in a 21 million square foot portfolio of office and retail portfolio. Oxford also managed 45 million square feet of commercial real estate properties located coast to coast in Canada.
"From Oxford's perspective they also get the management of the properties, which helps to augment their returns," said HSBC's Hough. "An acquisition like Prudential could be fairly positive."
